overview.oneLineTake: Soft jobs bought a record close, but rising yields, live oil risk, and Fed minutes ahead make this a fragile tape to sell premium into, not a reset.
themes: Soft September payrolls (+29K, negative revisions, unemployment 4.2%) killed October hike odds: Nasdaq 100 closed at a record Friday (QQQ +1.0% to 749.58, SPY +0.7% to 769.64), Nvidia hit a new high and AMD crossed $1T.

Bonds did not buy the relief: yields rose despite the weak print, the 10-year sits near 5.24% at 24-year highs, and 30-year mortgages jumped to about 7.3%. French spread stress and gilt highs keep the global rates reset live.

Energy shock stays live: more tankers struck near Iran, U.S. bombers pulled from a UK base on terror concerns, and Iraq is routing a supertanker through Hormuz. OPEC+ held November quotas and the G7 diesel release only eases the refining squeeze at the margin.
Fed risk has shifted from October to December: inflation is still outrunning wages, and this week's minutes are the next read on the Warsh board.
Earnings season opens (Delta, Pepsi, Levi's) while Paramount's $52B debt sale shows higher rates biting corporate borrowers.
risks: Long-end yields pushing further above 5% with equities at records sets up a rates-driven de-rating, with vol-control funds near record equity exposure as an amplifier.
Iran and Hormuz escalation lifts oil and diesel and re-feeds hike pricing.
Brazil's election (Bolsonaro early lead in the count) is an EM and FX swing risk at today's open.
Hawkish minutes revive December hike pricing and hit narrow AI and chip leadership.

nq.summary: Soft payrolls (+29K, negative revisions, UE 4.2%) cooled hike bets and pushed NDX to a record, and NQ is holding the gain overnight. The catch is the bond market: 10Y dipped to 5.16% on the print and closed 5.28%. Trend is up, but every leg higher is borrowing against yields. Thesis: mild long, 5/10 conviction (brief rated Low-Med); buy pullbacks to the old high, don't chase gaps. Invalidation: NDX close below 30,737.
nq.primaryCatalyst: ISM Services at 9:00 PM BKK (f 55.1 / p 55.4); watch prices paid.
nq.primaryRisk: 10Y breaking 5.30% or hawkish FOMC minutes (Thu 1:00 AM BKK).
nq.overnight: Globex opened firm, NQ +0.22% in a tight 31,059-31,169 band. No weekend shock to price.
nq.macro: Weak jobs moved the Fed path from October to December, but long-end yields rose anyway. A 10Y above 5.30% is the main de-rating threat for long-duration tech. Iran/Hormuz tanker headlines keep the oil-to-inflation channel live.
nq.volatility: VIX 15.3 (-6.6%), VXN 21.2 (-5.8%). Vol sold into the record, so dips can get bought until rates bite. Dealer gamma unavailable.
